Introduction to Statistics

Statistics for nurses — scales of measurement, data presentation, central tendency, dispersion and normal distribution.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe scales of measurement
  • Present data using tables and graphs
  • Calculate central tendency and dispersion
  • Describe the normal distribution and normalising data

In simple words

Statistics is the science of collecting, organising and making sense of numbers. It turns raw data into clear findings and supports decisions.

Scales of measurement

Scale Example What can be done
Nominal Gender, blood group Count only
Ordinal Pain mild, moderate, severe Rank or order
Interval Temperature in degrees Add and subtract, no true zero
Ratio Height, weight, pulse All arithmetic; true zero exists

Presenting data

  • Frequency table — categories with counts and percentages
  • Bar chart — compares categories
  • Histogram — shows shape of a continuous variable
  • Pie chart — shares of a total
  • Line graph — trends over time
  • Scatter plot — relationship between two numbers
  • Normal curve — symmetrical bell-shape with mean, median and mode equal

Central tendency

Measure Formula Use
Mean Sum of values / number of values Normal or interval data
Median Middle value Skewed data
Mode Most frequent value Nominal data

Dispersion

  • Range = highest value minus lowest
  • Variance = average squared distance from the mean
  • Standard deviation (SD) = square root of variance
  • About 95% of values fall within 2 SD of the mean in a normal distribution

Normal distribution

  • Symmetrical bell-shape; mean, median and mode coincide
  • 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD
  • Skewed data use the median; extreme values pull the mean

🔴 Choose the statistic from the level of data

Nominal data give mode; interval and ratio data give mean and SD. The level of measurement decides which test is allowed — using a mean for a nominal variable is meaningless.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Four scales: nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio.
  2. The mean is the average; the median is the middle; the mode is most frequent.
  3. Standard deviation measures the spread of values.
  4. In a normal distribution mean, median and mode are equal.
  5. About 95% of values fall within 2 SD of the mean.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Skewed data are better represented by the median.
  2. The bar chart compares categories; the histogram shows distribution.
  3. The mode is the only measure of central tendency for numbers.
  4. The pie chart shows parts of the total.
  5. Interpreting statistics needs both significance and clinical meaning.

📌 Memory trick

Central tendency: M-M-M — Mean, Median, Mode.

60-second revision

  • Scales: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio.
  • Presentation: tables, bar, histogram, pie, line, scatter.
  • Central tendency: mean, median, mode.
  • Dispersion: range, variance, standard deviation.
  • Normal distribution: 68-95-99.7 rule.

Test yourself

Gender and blood group are measured on which scale?

Answer: A. Gender and blood group are nominal categories with no order.

The middle value of an ordered data set is the:

Answer: B. The median is the middle value in an ordered list.

About 68% of values in a normal distribution fall within:

Answer: A. In a normal distribution 68% of values lie within 1 SD of the mean, 95% within 2 SD.

Weight is measured on which scale?

Answer: D. Weight has a true zero and permits all arithmetic, so it is a ratio scale.

A bar chart is best for comparing:

Answer: A. Bar charts compare values across categories.
